title: The gradient speed check fails now and then on a busy machine
goal: One of the automated speed checks says a gradient must not cost much more to draw than a plain colour. On a busy machine it sometimes fails by a hair, which makes the whole test run go red for a reason that has nothing to do with what changed. The check should be measured in a way that does not depend on how loaded the machine is.
notes: Tests/PhotonzRenderTests/GradientPerfTests.swift:74, aGradientCostsWhatAFlatColorCostsOnceItIsDrawn. Seen 2026-09-04: cost 53.9ms against a threshold of flat*3+10 = 52.7ms, so it missed by 2 percent; four other runs of the same commit passed. Both sides are best-of-5 wall clock on the same machine, so a scheduling hiccup during the gradient half alone tips it. Options: take the best of more rounds, interleave the flat and gradient measurements so both see the same load, or measure CPU time the way ElementBounds perf tests do.
acceptance: Ten runs of Scripts/test.sh in a row all pass on a machine that is also building something else
The check still fails if a gradient really does cost many times what a plain colour costs
The failure message still says what it measured and against what
